messages:
Maria (eng-infra): Heads up — multiple gRPC stream stalls observed between pods on different nodes in us-west-2. Seen on model-serving and redispatch services.
Ben (eng-sre): Can you paste an example trace? service + pod pair + times?
Maria (eng-infra): model-serving pod/replica-2 -> redispatch pod/replica-7, around 21:37 UTC. Long tail at ~9–12s then stream reset. tcp retransmits and RST seen.
Oliver (net): Any pattern by AZ or node pair? VXLAN/GENEVE in use?
Maria (eng-infra): Mostly cross-node same-AZ, a couple inter-AZ. We use Cilium with VXLAN overlay on those nodes.
Thao (runtime): I pulled tcpdump from the client node:
```
IP (tos 0x0, id 0, frag 0, proto TCP (6), length 1514)
  10.2.3.45.50256 > 10.2.8.11.8080: Flags [P.], seq 1:1465, ack 1, win 501, length 1464
IP (tos 0x0, id 0, frag 0, proto TCP (6), length 250)
  (fragmented IP packet)
```
Looks like fragmentation + reassembly happening.
Ben (eng-sre): That length 1514 suggests outer encap + payload hitting >1500 MTU. Path MTU discovery would normally avoid fragmentation, but overlay encap reduces available MTU.
Oliver (net): Agree — VXLAN adds ~50 bytes. If node NIC MTU left at 1500, inner packets get fragmented. GSO/GRO can mask on host but breaks with some routers/rdma paths. Also seen issues where offloads produce large skbs that get dropped mid-path.
infra-oncall: quick check — node-43/44 show ethtool offload stats w/ high GSO coalesced segments.
Maria (eng-infra): Any quick mitigations? We need immediate reduction in streaming errors.
Oliver (net): Options: 1) Lower overlay MTU (Cilium/VXLAN) to 1400/1450 to account for encap, 2) Clamp MSS on LB and service egress, 3) disable GSO/GRO on affected NICs as hotfix (ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off), 4) enable vxlan_udp_csum or similar if fragmentation is problematic.
Thao (runtime): We tested disabling GSO on one node — gRPC streams stabilized but CPU went up ~8% on the envoy side. Not ideal long term.
Ben (eng-sre): Can we do a staged bump: update Cilium config to set tunnelMTU=1400 in helm values, roll the nodes in a canary rack?
Oliver (net): That's the least intrusive. Also double-check kube-proxy/netfilter doesn't re-MTU clamp unexpectedly.
Maria (eng-infra): I'll open a small canary with 3 nodes (model-serving pool). Can we prepare a runbook for rollback?
infra-oncall: I'll script the rollback (helm set back, cordon/uncordon) and a traffic-check script: `kubectl exec -it $CLIENT -- curl -sS --raw --no-buffer http://$SVC:8080/stream` to look for stalls.
deploy-bot: deployment model-serving updated: canary=3/3, rollout started at 21:59 UTC.
Ben (eng-sre): Also add kernel option to avoid silent PMTU blackhole temporarily: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=1` on canary nodes — but that prevents PMTU discovery (tradeoff). Use only if needed.
Thao (runtime): Note about RDMA: RDMA-enabled paths weren't showing stalls; traffic using kernel TCP/Envoy path is affected. That suggests overlay/GSO interplay not RDMA.
Maria (eng-infra): Canary nodes rolled with VXLAN MTU=1400. After ~10 minutes, streams look normal for canary traffic. No resets.
Oliver (net): Great. Next steps: plan cluster-wide MTU change during low-traffic window, verify CNI docs for recommended MTU when using cloud ENIs and IP-in-IP/VXLAN. Also monitor CPU after disabling offloads if we use that as fallback.
Ben (eng-sre): Add alert for gRPC stream reset rate and p50/p99 stream latency around load-balancer to catch regressions.
Maria (eng-infra): Thanks team — will schedule a maintenance window and run full rollout tomorrow 04:00 UTC. I'll paste final runbook here when ready. :thumbsup:
Oliver (net): And we should document the cause: overlay encapsulation + host MTU unchanged + GSO interactions causing fragments that some switches/paths drop -> gRPC stream stalls. Saves future debugging cycles.
Maria (eng-infra): Agreed. I'll create a concise postmortem + config snippets after rollout.
